newsitem.title: USA: Hunters easily shot if not easy to spot.
newsitem.headline: Hunters easily shot if not easy to spot.

text.p: Bright orange clothing can save your life if you're a hunter, the Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said Thursday.

It said hunters were more likely to be shot accidentally if they were not wearing bright orange clothing to make them easier to see. A study of 343 incidents in New York State between 1989 and 1995 showed that victims of accidental shootings were not wearing "hunter" orange clothing in 76 percent of the cases.
Forty states require hunters to wear fluorescent orange clothing to increase their visibility but New York is not one of them.

Instances where one hunter shot another accounted for 70 percent of 508 hunting-associated firearm injuries reported to the New York Department of Environmental Conservation between 1989 and 1995. Two-party incidents accounted for 79 percent of the 39 fatalities, the CDC said.
Hunters were most often injured when they were mistaken for game, the study found. None of the turkey hunters shot for this reason was wearing the recommended orange clothing.

The International Hunter Education Associated estimated there were 1,201 hunting injuries involving firearms during 1995, including 107 deaths. Of those injuries, 71 percent involved two parties, including 69 of the fatalities.
